subject.title: fix(opencode): public models work without configured credentials

question: Should OpenClaw support credentialless OpenCode Zen access for catalog models that OpenCode’s own client classifies as public, despite Zen’s current user documentation requiring an API key?
rationale: The code can implement either policy safely, but deciding whether an undocumented third-party anonymous mode is a supported OpenClaw provider contract is product and provider-ownership judgment rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Support the upstream-client contract
options.body: Accept the catalog-driven `public` key behavior for zero-input-cost models and retain the branch’s paid/unknown-model credential gate.

options.title: Require configured credentials
options.body: Keep the current OpenClaw policy until OpenCode publishes a stable Zen documentation or API contract for anonymous inference.

recommendation.title: Support the upstream-client contract
recommendation.body: Accept the catalog-driven `public` key behavior for zero-input-cost models and retain the branch’s paid/unknown-model credential gate.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor has the most direct implementation context, though a repository provider owner should make the final policy decision.
